transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-09-09 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~42m | Attendees: Lena, Marcus (Redwood); Raj, Aisha, Evan (Needle & Haystack)

[00:00] Lena: hey everybody, thanks for making time, i'm lena with redwood inference, i'm the account exec on this, with marcus our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Raj: good thanks, morning for us, thanks lena. excited to see what you have.
[00:12] Aisha: hi all, quick context — search relevance has been slipping since our catalog bump in june, looking for a low lift improvement that doesn't add multi-second tail latency.
[00:22] Marcus: right, great context. today we'll show the hosted embeddings flow plus a lightweight rerank endpoint — the idea is: first stage ANN retrieval with your vector store then call our reranker for final ordering, keeps latency tight but improves relevance.
[00:35] Evan: curious — what's typical p95 on rerank with hosted? we have a 200ms p95 budget.
[00:40] Marcus: typical p95 depends on model choice and sequence length, for our optimized rerank models we've seen 120-220ms p95 for single-shot rerank calls on our hosted tier. with batching you can push qps up but latency then trades off.
[00:52] Raj: batching meaning you group queries? that sounds like it might affect user facing latency.
[00:56] Marcus: exactly — batch window versus user latency. we can do micro-batching (20-40ms window) so often p95 stays in your target but cost drops 20-30%. redwood optimize will suggest batching config based on your traffic pattern.
[01:10] Aisha: can you show the actual API call? i want to see params for embeddings vs rerank.
[01:14] Marcus: yeah, i'll share the curl and the python snippet. so step one — POST /v1/embeddings with your doc text, we return fixed-dim vectors. step two, you do approximate nearest neighbor, then POST /v1/rerank with candidate snippets + user query. the rerank endpoint supports pairwise and pointwise modes, and you can ask for explanations.
[01:30] [Marcus screenshares, typing sounds]
[01:35] Marcus: here's a live curl: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" -d '{"input":"red shoes size 9"}' — returns vector. then for rerank: POST /v1/rerank body has query, candidates array, model param, return_scores true.
[01:50] Evan: and what's in the candidate payload? full doc text or snippet?
[01:53] Marcus: either. we recommend snippet+metadata to keep payload small; the model context window is used for candidate scoring. also we support KV cache and prefix caching to avoid recomputing embeddings for frequently requested docs — though that's more for generation flows it's available.
[02:10] Raj: data residency — our catalog is partially EU servers, we can't send full PII out of region. hosted will be in us-east or eu-west we saw on the docs, is there a region pin for customer?
[02:21] Lena: yes, hosted region pinning is supported; we can ensure inference stays in eu-west for EU-only datasets. for strict compliance you can also choose Dedicated or Private deployment which gives you VPC and on-prem options.
[02:33] Aisha: what's the difference again between Dedicated and Private? we've got a compliance review next week so need to understand.
[02:36] Marcus: Dedicated is reserved GPU pools in our cloud with tenant isolation and SLA — you still use our control plane. Private is where the control plane is in your VPC or on-prem package — full isolation and you manage keys, HSM/KMS. For SOC2 and enterprise audits both are compatible but Private gives you the highest control.
[02:55] Raj: any gotchas on SSO? we use saml with okta.
[02:58] Lena: we support SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning, we'll include the SSO setup guide in the follow up.
[03:04] Evan: ok demo please.
[03:07] [Marcus runs a sample request against a small toy dataset]
[03:12] Marcus: here's baseline — we ran a naive lexical search then passed top 10 to reranker. baseline mean reciprocal rank was 0.42; reranker bumped to 0.68 on our sample. i'll paste the notebook link in chat.
[03:25] Raj: nice, are those ground truth judgments?
[03:28] Marcus: the demo uses a small curated eval set, in a pilot we'd use your query logs to build more representative evals. the console has eval dashboards to track regressions overtime.
[03:37] [00:03:40] Lena: one thing i want to call out — Optimize will analyze token distribution and suggest quantization profiles for candidate reranker models which can cut inference cost ~40% with minimal quality drop. it's conservative and model-specific.
[03:55] Aisha: quantization on rerank models, sure, but does that change latency?
[03:58] Marcus: minor effect on latency, usually slightly faster on supported hardware. bigger wins are in throughput / cost.
[04:05] Evan: on the console can we see token-level cost per route?
[04:08] Marcus: yup. per-route token-cost breakdowns, per-model latencies, and tracing hooks so you can jump from a slow request to the raw request/response.
[04:18] Raj: what about model versioning? we want to be able to canary a new reranker.
[04:22] Marcus: built in — you can pin model versions, do canary rollouts, do A/B tests and set automatic fallback policies. the console shows a diff of eval metrics between versions.
[04:33] Aisha: you mentioned explanations — how do those look? are they token-level gradients or just saliency highlights?
[04:39] Marcus: currently we provide saliency-style highlights and candidate-level scores; for deeper introspection we can surface attention-weight-ish signals but those are approximate. it's mainly to help triage why something was demoted.
[04:52] Raj: any limitations on candidate size? we typically pass 30 candidates for diversity.
[04:56] Marcus: recommended is top 10-20 for latency but 30 is fine if you're okay with slightly higher tail. you can also do a hybrid approach: use reranker for top 10 and a cheap re-scoring heuristic for the rest.
[05:08] Evan: curious about cost math — can you ballpark tokens per rerank call?
[05:12] Marcus: tokens depend on text length; small snippets tend to be 50-150 tokens each. for 10 candidates + query you're looking at roughly 600-1500 tokens per call. multiply by your qps and model choice; we'll run a projection for your traffic in the follow up.
[05:28] Aisha: our main worry is A/B test causing regression in conversion; how do we surface quality regressions quickly?
[05:33] Marcus: console evals + continuous monitoring — you can tie eval sets to production query slices, get alerting on metric drift, and roll back automatically if quality drops below threshold.
[05:45] Raj: any offline tooling to simulate reranker without hitting live API?
[05:48] Marcus: yes — we provide a local eval harness and a sample notebook that uses your logs to run offline rerank experiments. it's included in the pilot package.
[05:58] [06:00] Lena: ok let's talk timeline and pricing quickly — what are you thinking for pilot scope?
[06:04] Raj: 30-day pilot, want to test on 10k queries/day, live traffic shadowing, goal is 5% lift in click-thru / conversion.
[06:12] Lena: that's reasonable. we'll propose a pilot that includes 1 dev seat, access to Hosted API in eu-west, 50k demo credits and assistance from our solutions team to wire the evals.
[06:22] Evan: for the pilot do we need a dedicated API key?
[06:25] Marcus: yes — we'll provision a scoped API key and show you how to rotate keys via the console.
[06:31] Aisha: encryption at rest and key mgmt — do you integrate with our KMS?
[06:34] Lena: for Hosted we manage keys but we support customer-managed keys via KMS for Dedicated and Private modes. we'll detail this in the security pack.
[06:44] Raj: ok anything else on the tech side?
[06:46] Marcus: a couple of implementation tips: 1) precompute doc embeddings and store in your vector DB; 2) use short snippets for candidate payloads; 3) enable prefix caching for frequently requested docs; 4) run Optimize's suggestions to pick quantization/model combos.
[06:58] Evan: that prefix caching detail — is that automatic or we have to instrument?
[07:02] Marcus: there is an automatic prefix/KV cache in the runtime but you can also instrument cache keys in your app for more control. note: the transcriber sometimes writes K V cache as separate words in older docs.
[07:15] Raj: last question — SLA for Hosted? we need 99.9% uptime for our consumer app.
[07:19] Lena: hosted tier has uptime commitments; Dedicated has stronger SLA options. we'll include the SLA table in the follow up.
[07:27] Aisha: cool. please send security docs and pilot proposal.
[07:30] Lena: will do. any other questions?
[07:33] Raj: no, that's it. thanks.
[07:35] Lena: great, thanks everyone. recap: lena sends pricing/pilot & compliance docs, marcus sends notebook + eval template, needle & haystack shares anonymized logs. target follow up: pilot kickoff week of 2026-09-20.
[07:50] Meeting ended.

Notes on transcript: occasional transcription errors ("sock two" for SOC2, "sammel" for SAML) present; proper nouns sometimes off (redwood product names abbreviated), natural crosstalk and filler words retained.
